claims.statement: Expected reduction in NWC in H2 FY25 on back of festive & wedding demand
Retail expansion plan of adding 650+ stores in next 3 years
Consolidated EBITDA margin was 13.9% in Q2 FY25 vs 17.9% in Q2 FY24
Branded textile EBITDA margin fell to 18.9% in Q2 FY25 from 22.2% in Q2 FY24 due to operating deleverage
Branded apparel EBITDA margin improved to 13% in Q2 FY25 from 12.1% in Q2 FY24
Garmenting EBITDA margin improved to 9.6% in Q2 FY25 from 7.5% in Q2 FY24
Garmenting segment has a healthy order book and expects strong growth in H2 FY25
Garmenting capacity expansion of INR200 crores underway, 50% implemented, balance over next 12 months to reach 10 million units capacity
Garmenting capacity expansion on track to become third largest suit maker worldwide upon completion
Targeting 200 additional stores over next 18 months, primarily asset-light franchising model, emphasizing Ethnix by Raymond
Ethnix by Raymond targeting 150 stores by end of Q3 FY25 and 180-200 stores by March 2025, 300+ stores over 2-3 years
Expect double-digit growth in branded apparel in H2 FY25 driven by wedding season and positive October retail trends
Plan to add 650+ stores in next 3 years
Target 20% reduction in scope 1 & 2 emissions by 2030
Target 20% renewable energy by 2030
Target Zero Liquid Discharge by 2030
Target 30% decrease in waste to landfill by 2030
Target 20% gender diversity by 2030
Target single digit employee turnover rate
Target 100% return to work rate
Management expects sustainable EBITDA margin of around 15% once retail expansion stabilizes, targeting full recovery in FY26.
Management expects gradual EBITDA margin recovery from current levels, with full recovery in FY26.
Management aspires to reach INR 2,200 crore EBITDA by FY28, but timing may shift by 12-18 months due to urban discretionary headwinds.
Consolidated EBITDA margin was 12.3% in Q3 FY25, down from prior year due to weak demand, scale deleverage, upfront investments, and adverse mix.
Branded textile EBITDA margin at 18% vs 21.6% last year, impacted by scale deleverage.
Branded apparel EBITDA margin at 9.6% vs 13.9% last year, due to upfront retail expansion and advertising spends.
Garmenting EBITDA margin at 7.8% vs 11.3% last year, hit by product mix from new clients, Red Sea freight costs, and blue-collar training costs.
High-value cotton shirting EBITDA margin stood at 10.3% in Q3 FY25.
Management targets branded textile EBITDA margin of 20-21% steady state, branded apparel 13-14% over time, garmenting back to double-digit, blending to ~15% consolidated.
Bookings for suiting, shirting, fabrics and apparel AW25 season are underway and showing positive trend, giving confidence for FY26 growth.
Retail store expansion is a ~36-month journey; ~12-13 months in, another 20-24 months to reach threshold store levels, calibrated to environment.
Garmenting capacity expansion underway; once complete, company expects to become third largest suit maker worldwide.
India-UK FTA signed, seen as vital for integrating India into resilient global value chains
Expect FY26 to be a year of recovery with growth trajectory returning; early bookings show 12-13% growth vs last year
Branded Textile steady-state margin range 20-22%; overall lifestyle business decent margin 14-15%
Autumn winter 2025 bookings for Branded Textile are decent; overall bookings up 12-13% vs last year
Garmenting capacity expansion underway; once complete will be one of largest suit makers worldwide
Early festive likely to drive strong bookings in Branded Textiles; expecting robust volume growth
Improving order book in Garmenting business in H2; focus on lowering customer concentration risks
Calibrated approach on opening of new stores: through FOFO route and marquee locations
FY26 expected to be a strong recovery year with promising forward bookings for Autumn-Winter '26 collection
FY26 capex budget of Rs 175-200 crores with 55-60% maintenance capex, Rs 40-45 crores for garmenting expansion in Andhra Pradesh, balance for IT upgrades
Strong double-digit growth in Autumn-Winter '26 bookings for both fabric and apparel segments
Garmenting line expansion continuing in Andhra Pradesh, Ethiopia facility at lowest tariff rate of 10% may ramp up production to service US demand
Festive season likely to drive strong bookings in Branded Textiles; expecting robust volume growth
Continue increased marketing spends during festive season for improved brand visibility
Focus on profitability improvements led by operating leverage and enhancing efficiencies

Consolidated EBITDA margin 13.9% in Q2 FY26 vs 13.9% YoY; branded textile margin 20% vs 18.9% YoY; branded apparel margin 5.2% vs 13% YoY due to marketing spend and new stores; garmenting export margin 5.4% vs 9.6% YoY due to US tariffs
Strong bookings for winter and summer seasons in branded textile; booking growth 8-10% with improved product mix; dealers voluntarily pre-poning deliveries and picking from ex-stock

Focus on capacity utilization across five manufacturing plants; running plants at full or near-full capacity to reduce per-unit costs; confident of good utilization over next few quarters based on fabric bookings
Five manufacturing facilities; targeting high capacity utilization driven by strong fabric bookings for upcoming quarters

Branded apparel targeting INR2,300-2,500 crores annual revenue for early double-digit margins; expects 2-2.5 years to reach that scale; Ethnix UK sales INR150 crores annually, potential to double in 2-2.5 years post-FTA enactment
Selective store additions in branded apparel; focus on franchisee-run stores; will not miss marquee mall opportunities; existing store profitability priority over expansion
Management declined to provide medium-term revenue growth and margin guidance for branded textiles
Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded from 12.3% to 14.4% year-on-year; 9-month margin improved from 11.6% to 12.5%
Garmenting export order book impacted by US tariff uncertainty; US market dependency reduced from 50% to 35%
Branded textile facility utilized at full capacity; garmenting capacity can generate at least 50% more revenue from current levels
FY27 focus on premiumization across all segments, casualization, GTM expansion, geography diversification, holistic marketing
FY27 target: double-digit top-line growth and double-digit bottom-line growth; bottom-line to grow faster than top-line
FY27 store plan: gross addition of >100 EBOs, net addition of 30-40 stores
FY27 capex similar to FY26 (~INR180 cr); FY26 breakup: INR50 cr SAP, INR60 cr Hyderabad garmenting factory, balance stores & plant maintenance
Factory utilizations now above 90% (some 95%+), up from traditional 80-85%, driving opex reduction
Garmenting Q1 FY27 order books completely full; booking latter half of Q2 now
Branded Apparel core four brands EBITDA margin 7.8% (excl. emerging businesses); target double-digits in 2 years
Emerging businesses FY26: INR140 cr revenue, INR30 cr loss; will be reported separately from next quarter
Sleepwear segment annual EBITDA drag ~INR20 cr; provisions taken in FY26
FY27 Target: Double digit top line & higher double digit EBITDA growth
Order book full till December; booking for Q4 (January onwards) underway
Aim to at least double turnover in 5 years and grow EBITDA faster than topline
Expect 5-7% ASP hike in apparel and 7-9% in fabric for FY27
Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.6%, up 40 bps YoY
Garmenting EBITDA margin 7.3% vs -4.1% YoY, 1100 bps improvement
Target mid-teens ROCE for manufacturing-driven business over time
New factory in Andhra Pradesh; five garmenting factories total (3 Karnataka, 1 Andhra, 1 Ethiopia)
FY27 target: double digit top line and higher double digit EBITDA growth
FY27 roadmap focused on premiumization, casualization and geographical diversification
Manufacturing capacity: 43 Mn sqm fabric at Vapi, Chindwara, Jalgaon; 23 Mn sqm at Amravati, Kolhapur; 8.4 Mn pieces at Bangalore, Hindupur; 1.7 Mn pieces at Ethiopia
FY27 guidance: double-digit top-line growth, mid-double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 cr+ net cash, double-digit PBT growth
FY27 closing targets: double-digit revenue growth, mid-high double-digit EBITDA growth, ~INR300 cr FCFF, PBT ~INR220-225 cr
Garmenting plants at 90%+ utilisation; adding 7 lines at Hindupur (total 10 lines); peak capacity ~10 mn units/year; 3 lines live, 4th by Dec, rest over 18-20 months
Garmenting order book robust; factories booked till Jan-end/Feb 10-15; now booking for end-Feb; Europe inquiries up 30% H1 YoY, 50% Q2 YoY
Consolidated Q2 EBITDA margin 12.7% (-120 bps YoY); H1 11%; H2 expected >12.7% on scale, price pass-through, cost cuts; full-year mid-double-digit EBITDA growth
Branded Apparel Q2 margin 8.8% (flat YoY); expect double-digit plus in 2 years; Q3 benefit from fresh stock at new prices, store closures, operating leverage
High Value Cotton Shirting Q2 margin 9.5% (-200+ bps YoY); flax prices stabilising, newer orders at higher prices, plant cost cuts; expect double-digit plus EBITDA by year-end
